_meta.purpose: Japanese flood-control interventions, each matched to ward attributes by hard constraints so different wards get different recommendations.
_meta.confidence_note: Effectiveness is given as qualitative bands (high/medium/low), not invented percentages. Every entry names a real place and operator.

real_example.name: Kanda River / Loop Road No. 7 Underground Regulating Reservoir, Tokyo
real_example.operator: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Bureau of Construction

interventions.mechanism: A large tunnel beneath an arterial road stores stormwater during peak flow and releases it slowly afterwards. No surface land needed.
interventions.india_relevance: Fits dense zones on wide arterial corridors where no surface land is available — much of Hyderabad's core.

real_example.name: G-Cans, Kasukabe, Saitama (world's largest)
real_example.operator: MLIT Kanto Regional Bureau, Edogawa River Office

interventions.mechanism: Giant deep tunnels and silos divert overflow from multiple rivers, storing it and pumping it to a large river after the storm. A basin-scale megaproject.
interventions.india_relevance: A long-term basin-scale option for the worst-hit riverfront zones along the Musi.

real_example.name: Tsurumi River Multipurpose Retention Basin, Yokohama (sports fields in dry weather)

interventions.mechanism: A large low-lying open area (park, playing fields) deliberately floods during storms to hold water, then drains and returns to public use.
interventions.india_relevance: Suits large peripheral wards that still have open ground near the river.

interventions.mechanism: Shallow deliberate ponding on existing public ground (school grounds, small parks) shaves the runoff peak. Cheap, uses land you already have.
interventions.india_relevance: Fast, low-cost option deployable in almost any ward with a school or park.

real_example.name: Sumida City rainwater storage ordinance, Tokyo

interventions.mechanism: A municipal ordinance requires new buildings to hold rainwater on-site in tanks, releasing it slowly. Distributed storage across a dense area.
interventions.india_relevance: Policy lever for dense built-up wards where large works are impossible.

interventions.mechanism: Porous road and footpath surfaces let rain soak into the ground instead of running off, cutting the volume that reaches drains.
interventions.india_relevance: Best on flat wards with mild-to-moderate flooding; retrofit during road resurfacing.

interventions.mechanism: Roadside pits and planted gardens capture runoff and let it percolate into the soil, reducing peak flow into drains.
interventions.india_relevance: Cheap distributed measure for mild-flooding residential wards.

real_example.name: Arakawa Super Levee, Tokyo
real_example.operator: MLIT Kanto Regional Bureau, Arakawa-Karyu River Office

interventions.mechanism: A very wide, gently sloped embankment that resists overtopping and breach, doubling as developable land on top. Protects riverfront zones.
interventions.india_relevance: For Musi-front wards where breach and overtopping are the flood mechanism.

interventions.mechanism: Widening and deepening the river channel raises how much flow it can carry before spilling into adjacent land.
interventions.india_relevance: Direct fix for Musi-adjacent wards where channel capacity is the bottleneck.

interventions.mechanism: Small barriers on steep upstream channels trap sediment and slow torrent flow, reducing downstream debris flooding. Japan's signature export.
interventions.india_relevance: Only for the few steeper, rocky wards on the city's western/northern edge.

real_example.name: Nationwide municipal hazard maps under the Flood Control Act

interventions.mechanism: Every municipality must publish flood-risk maps so residents and planners know exposure and evacuation routes. Non-structural, universal.
interventions.india_relevance: A no-regret first step deployable in every ward immediately.

interventions.mechanism: A dense radar network delivers minute-scale, street-scale rainfall nowcasts for early warning and drainage operation. Warning, not prevention.
interventions.india_relevance: City-wide early-warning backbone; pairs with GHMC's emergency response.

real_example.name: Japan's nationwide Ryuiki Chisui basin flood-control policy (2020-)

interventions.mechanism: Coordinates every actor across a whole river basin — storage, land use, forecasting — rather than defending each stretch alone. A planning framework.
interventions.india_relevance: The umbrella framework for whole-of-Musi planning across all riverfront wards.

real_example.name: Tsurumi River comprehensive flood control, since 1980

interventions.mechanism: Combines structural works with land-use control and on-site storage across a fast-urbanising basin — the model JICA used in Chennai.
interventions.india_relevance: Precedented in India via JICA's Chennai master-plan work; fits dense urbanised wards.
